issues.body: The pre-registration says KILL 3 fires when hedging regresses abstention precision, but `verdict_for` only tests trap-subset recall-like scores plus mean ordinary-task answer accuracy. `acc_non_regression` is not equivalent to abstention precision: if baseline ordinary accuracy is low, the treatment may add false-positive abstentions on answerable tasks while keeping mean ordinary score at or above baseline, and can still satisfy `quality_superior` and be recommended. The output also exposes no abstention precision/recall values, despite declaring that axis. The current synthetic success fixture has no false-positive abstentions, so it does not catch this omission.
issues.fix_hint: For the hedging capability, compute TP/FP/FN from structured abstention decisions across trap and ordinary tasks, report treatment and baseline precision/recall, and add an explicit no-regression precision condition to KILL 3 and `recommend_adopt`. Add a synthetic test where treatment trap recall improves but false-positive abstentions make precision worse; it must fire KILL 3 and refuse adoption.
issues.title: Hedging adoption does not measure or gate abstention precision

verdict.summary: The analyzer is thoughtfully structured and its synthetic tests cover most declared honesty gates and kill paths, but the hedging decision does not implement one of the pre-registered load-bearing quality criteria. It can recommend adoption even when abstention precision regresses, so the emitted verdict is not yet sound as scoped.
